channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Open New Border Post 'Keskanyor' with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to open the 'Keskanyor' border post, twice the size of 'Dostlik', with Kyrgyzstan. An agreement has been reached, with project development and construction to begin within three months. This aims to triple cargo volume and halve transit times. Additionally, construction of a paid Tashkent-Andijan highway is slated to start in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Science and Technology
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a working meeting to discuss scientific and technological cooperation, including joint initiatives within the 'One Belt, One Road' and SCO frameworks. Key areas include water resources, ecology, climate change, and digital technologies. Both sides explored possibilities for joint research projects and academic exchanges.

item.title: 19 Kazakh servicemen swept away at Caspian Sea training exercise
item.description: Nineteen Kazakh servicemen were swept away during a training exercise near the Caspian Sea coast. Nine individuals have died, and three have been rescued. The incident occurred during drills on the Caspian Sea shore.

item.title: Money changer killed by unidentified gunmen in Afghanistan's Ghazni province
item.description: Local sources reported that a money changer, identified as Gulbuddin, was shot dead by unknown gunmen in the Wali Dad village of Qarabagh district, Ghazni province. The man was inside his vehicle when the attack occurred. His father reportedly works for the Taliban police headquarters in Ghazni.

item.title: Tajikistan Defense Minister Demands Quality Autumn Conscription
item.description: Tajikistan's Defense Minister, Colonel General Emomali Sobirzoda, has called for a high-quality autumn conscription drive. The directive was issued during a methodological training meeting focused on preparing for the conscription of citizens into the armed forces. Favorable service conditions were also highlighted.

item.title: UN General Assembly Discusses Artificial Intelligence Risks and Control
item.description: Artificial intelligence was a key topic at the UN General Assembly's 81st session, with world leaders warning about autonomous weapons, disinformation, and job losses. Disagreements emerged on control, with the US favoring competition and others calling for international rules and state oversight.

item.title: Andijan to Establish Special Fund for Women's Employment with $20 Million
item.description: A special fund will be established in Andijan to ensure women's employment, with $20 million allocated. This initiative aims to create separate financial and organizational opportunities for women's employment in the region.

item.title: Regional Competition for Female Civil Servants Held in Dangara District
item.description: A regional tour of the Republican Competition 'Best Female Civil Servant' took place in Dangara district on September 22, 2026. Participants were assessed on political knowledge, legal education, professional skills, and communication etiquette, reflecting state policy to enhance women's role in public service.

item.title: Andijan to Invest 100 Billion Soums in Fruit and Vegetable Processing
item.description: Andijan plans to allocate 100 billion soums for fruit and vegetable processing, aiming to reach a 30% processing level by providing small processing equipment to the public on lease, as decided in a presidential meeting.

item.title: Taliban spokesman: Pakistani airstrikes killed four civilians in Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid stated that four civilians were killed in Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces. He condemned the attacks as a "blatant act of aggression" and vowed they would not go unanswered. Pakistan's information minister claimed the strikes were in response to drones entering Pakistani territory.

item.title: Central Asia Internet Connectivity Forum CAPIF 5 kicks off in Dushanbe
item.description: The fifth Central Asia Connectivity and Peering Forum (CAPIF 5) began in Dushanbe on September 24, 2026. This is the first time the event is held in Tajikistan. The forum brings together internet community representatives, providers, operators, IXPs, government bodies, and IT specialists from Central Asia and beyond to discuss network connectivity and internet infrastructure development.

item.title: Andijan to free up 30 administrative buildings for business development
item.description: Andijan will repurpose 30 administrative buildings for business use, freeing up 13 hectares of land and 70,000 square meters of space. This initiative, involving the relocation of state organizations to the city of Bobur, is expected to attract $1 billion in investments.

item.title: Germany offers 800 nursing positions for Uzbek healthcare workers
item.description: Uzbekistan's mid-level healthcare professionals are invited to work in German clinics through the Globogate program, which offers 800 job openings. Participants will receive 10 months of free German language courses, covering tuition, accommodation, and B2 certification. All visa, travel, and transfer costs are also covered.

item.title: World Bank: Security spending exceeds other sectors in Taliban administration
item.description: A World Bank report indicates that security spending by the Taliban administration has reached 45.2% of total expenditures this fiscal year. This amount surpasses combined spending on education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, and private sector development. The report also notes a slowdown in Afghanistan's economic momentum.

item.title: Tajikistan and FAO discuss food safety and agricultural development
item.description: Tajikistan's Committee for Food Security met with FAO representatives to discuss strengthening cooperation in food safety and agricultural production. Key topics included livestock health, inter-sectoral collaboration, animal disease prevention, and the 'One Health' principles. Discussions also covered plant protection and digitalization in the agricultural sector.

item.title: Zelenskyy tells UN Putin is a 'zero patient' spreading war, urges peace talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the UN, calling Russian President Vladimir Putin a 'zero patient' spreading the idea of war. He emphasized the need for peace, stating that decisions on the battlefield should not determine outcomes. Zelenskyy highlighted Russia's territorial ambitions despite its vast landmass.

item.title: European Council President stresses freedom of navigation through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa urged Iran to cooperate with the IAEA and end attacks on neighbors, stressing freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasized dialogue for peace and stated the EU is ready to support diplomatic efforts to resolve tensions with the US.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 1.1 Billion Som Embezzled in Liquid Soap Purchase in Samarqand
item.description: Officials in the School Education Department of Samarqand region purchased liquid soap at inflated prices, leading to the embezzlement of 1.1 billion som in budget funds. A criminal case has been initiated under Article 167 of the Criminal Code for embezzlement. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: CENTCOM Reports 115 Commercial Vessels Rerouted Due to Iran Naval Blockade
item.description: The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) reported that 115 commercial vessels were forced to reroute in regional waters as part of a naval blockade of Iran. This action aims to enforce the blockade, which was launched in response to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: National Ecology Committee: No environmental assessment for National Library parking project
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change stated there is no environmental assessment for a parking lot project near the National Library. The committee emphasized that construction and landscaping activities require proper ecological evaluation. It noted that planting new trees cannot fully replace the ecological value of existing mature ones.

item.title: Taliban report over 300 families forcibly returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 354 families, totaling 1,560 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan on the previous day. According to a Taliban deputy spokesman, Hamdullah Fitrat, these families entered through various border crossings, including Torkham in Nangarhar, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, Silk Bridge in Nimroz, and Islam Qala in Herat.

item.title: UN builds 35 climate-resilient greenhouses for farmers in central Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Development Programme (UNDP) has established 35 climate-resilient greenhouses for farmers in central Afghanistan, creating employment for 225 people, including 105 women. These greenhouses utilize water-efficient technologies to increase agricultural production, strengthen food security, and provide sustainable income, helping farmers cope with climate change impacts.

item.title: Lithuania temporarily halts work permit applications from Tajikistan and Central Asia
item.description: Lithuania has temporarily suspended applications for work permits and entry for citizens of Tajikistan and other Central Asian countries. The decision, announced by the head of Lithuania's Migration Department, is due to a significant increase in labor migrants from the region.

item.title: Pakistan confirms airstrikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan following drone incursions
item.description: Pakistan confirmed conducting precision aerial and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan, targeting sites used for launching drones. The strikes followed alleged "deliberate and unlawful incursions" by drones from Afghan territory. Local sources reported strikes in Khost, Kandahar, and Paktia provinces, with no casualties reported by the Taliban governor's spokesman in Khost.

item.title: Iran Airlines Cancel Flights Amidst US Sanctions Threat
item.description: Iranian airlines have reportedly canceled flights as US sanctions loom. One Iranian flight landed in Shanghai despite the threat of US sanctions.

item.title: Pakistan Attacks 10 Points in Afghanistan; Taliban Claims No Casualties
item.description: Pakistan launched attacks on 10 locations in Afghanistan. The Taliban reported that the strikes did not result in any casualties.

item.title: New technologies double cotton yield at Agrocluster Oltingul
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agrocluster Oltingul has doubled cotton yields using Xinjiang technology on 23 hectares of its 850-hectare fields. This method, involving double-row planting under film and drip irrigation, saves water by 40% and fertilizer by 30%. The initiative aligns with a December 2025 presidential decree aimed at boosting crop yields and resource efficiency in agriculture.

item.title: UNDP Constructs 205 Earthquake-Resistant Buildings in Nangarhar with South Korean Aid
item.description: The UNDP has built 205 earthquake-resistant buildings in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, with support from South Korea. The structures include homes and health centers, with 203 housing vulnerable families. The project also created jobs for 719 locals and restored irrigation for 500 acres of farmland.

item.title: Artificial intelligence center for youth established in Balykchy
item.description: An artificial intelligence center for youth has been established in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, following a presidential decree. The center, created by "Akademiya IT Star," aims to develop digitalization services export and provide IT training in marketing, programming, and robotics. It has created 100 jobs and offers IT services to over 500 businesses.

item.title: Intensive technologies boost fish farming efficiency in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A fish farming project utilizing intensive technologies has been launched by "Chinobod real biznes" in Balykchy district, Kyrgyzstan. The project, costing 30 billion soms, produces 200 tons of fish meat and 2.5 million fry annually on a two-hectare area. It also includes a laboratory for water purification using chlorella.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva attends UN session, holds meetings in New York
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. She held bilateral meetings with the CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to discuss joint projects in transport and healthcare, and with Google's Vice President regarding YouTube monetization.

item.title: Central Asian Experts Discuss Future of Regional Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: An international expert meeting on Central Asia's independent strategies, regional security, and new cooperation formats was held in Cadenabbia, Italy. Organized by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the event gathered experts from the region to discuss what shapes Central Asian identity and the future of regional partnerships.

item.title: Balykchy Enterprise Produces Sports Equipment Meeting International Standards
item.description: The 'LB Sport' enterprise in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, manufactures sports equipment according to international standards, replacing imports. The project, costing 25 billion soums, produces 65 types of equipment for 18 sports, with an annual output of 500,000 units worth 75 billion soums. Exports reach $3 million annually to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and CIS countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan actively prepares for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively preparing for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum, scheduled for September 28-29 in Tashkent and Samarkand. The forum will focus on human rights, sustainable development, and international cooperation, marking anniversaries of key human rights pacts and declarations.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets Residents and Entrepreneurs on Andijan Gastronomy Street
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged with residents and entrepreneurs on Andijan's gastronomy street in the Orikzor neighborhood. The 1.2-kilometer street created 100 new jobs and can accommodate over 10,000 visitors daily.

item.title: Two Afghan Citizens Enter US Via Legal Exception to Refugee Policy
item.description: Afghan Evacuate (AfghanIOM) reports two Afghan citizens entered the US through a legal exception to current policies, utilizing the refugee admission program. AfghanIOM's director stated this admission served US national interests. Thousands of Afghans await resettlement.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev visits ecotourism complex in Asaka
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited an ecotourism complex in Asaka. Once fully operational, the facility is expected to provide 80 billion soums in services annually and contribute 3 billion soums to the local budget.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Dies of Poisoning in Istanbul After Unofficial Treatment
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, Mohirano Meliyeva, died in Istanbul on September 19 due to poisoning from pharmaceutical agents. She was being treated at home by unofficial doctors, which worsened her condition. Despite being taken to hospital, doctors could not save her life. Her body was repatriated.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Reviews Xinjiang Cotton Growing Method Using Drip Irrigation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the Xinjiang method of cotton cultivation, which uses drip irrigation and fertilization systems to deliver water and nutrients directly to the plant roots. This method reportedly saves up to 40% of water and nearly 30% of fertilizer.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Learn About Eco-Friendly Heating Systems
item.description: An informational meeting was held in Bishkek for residents interested in eco-friendly and energy-efficient heating systems, specifically heat pumps. Participants learned about preferential state loans for installation, equipment costs, and operational benefits, including during electricity supply restrictions. The project is supported by the World Bank.
